J07.note: Verification vocabulary is mostly plain, but fixture framing overclaims, machine IDs lead titles, labels repeat and source prose is unedited.

J12.note: en-US only; copy is message-backed, dates are locale-formatted, and a notice explains that texts stay in their published language.

findings.where: /museum/network-onchain and every record route · default · all viewports · en-US
findings.observation: The banner on every page says 'read from a Sepolia test registry and IPFS', the intro says every item 'was fetched from IPFS and shown only after its hash matched the one the Museum stored in a test registry', and each record says 'Verified: these are the exact bytes the Museum recorded on-chain'. The build reads local fixtures. The only plain statement ('Read from local test fixtures ... not from the chain') sits at the foot of the index inside How this is checked. The contract checks (code hash, interface, owner is 'the Museum's test Safe', declaration, record count) show a green Passed beside a contract that is not read.
findings.consequence: A reviewer reads the top of any page as evidence that the registry was read and a contract checked, when neither happened. The page claims on-chain verification it does not perform.
findings.change: While the build reads fixtures: change the banner to 'Preview from local test fixtures. Not read from Sepolia or Ethereum mainnet.'; make the intro say the records come from the release's fixtures and are checked against the hashes in the release; drop 'recorded on-chain' from the Verified line; render the contract checks as 'Not checked: fixture' or hide them until a contract is read. Keep the existing live wording behind the registry-present branch.
findings.acceptance_check: With fixtures, the banner, intro, Verified line and contract checks on index and record pages state that nothing was read from a chain; no Passed mark appears for a contract check that was not run; the live branch copy is unchanged.

findings.where: record routes and index Releases section · default · all viewports · en-US
findings.observation: On-chain facts carries the line 'The values the registry stores for this record, as stored.' Under it every record shows Published 'Nov 23, 2026, 00:00 UTC' (identical on all 13 record pages, and the release row says 'Sealed Nov 23, 2026, 00:00 UTC'), a Sequence, a Publisher address and 'Bytes served by: fixture'. These are fixture values, not registry storage, yet Published and Sealed present as chain timestamps.
findings.consequence: Synthesized publication dates and sequence numbers read as real on-chain history that a reviewer would cite.
findings.change: In fixture mode label the block 'Values from the fixture' and show Published, Sealed, Sequence and Publisher as 'Not on-chain yet' or omit them; keep 'as stored' for live reads only.
findings.acceptance_check: No record page or release row shows a Published or Sealed time, or the 'as stored' line, unless the value came from the registry.

findings.where: record-text-essay, texts, record-observation, record-declaration · default · all viewports · en-US
findings.observation: Implementation and machine identifiers appear as visible content: 'Source path records/accessions/6529NM.2026.001/public/casey-reas-collection-essay.md' (a repository file path); 'Bytes served by fixture'; text group headings '6529NM-PG-2026-001' and '6529NM-PG-2026-002'; text titles 'WP-3 source register' and 'WP-1 schema and vocabulary dependencies'; the observation titled 'Status observation 6529NM-WAVE-OBS-2026-08-08-001' whose 'What was observed' is a raw URL with two UUIDs; declaration 'Museum ID: declaration'; 'Canonical form ... RFC8785_JCS' repeating the code beside its name.
findings.consequence: Visitors meet working-package codes and file paths as headings and titles and cannot tell what 6529NM-PG-2026-001 or WP-3 is.
findings.change: Drop Source path from the visible fields (keep it in the copyable JSON). Name the proposed-gift groups by the work, e.g. 'Proposed gift: Conflict at Its Edges' and 'Proposed gift: Themes and Variations #210'. Title observations by what they observed ('Status observation, 8 Aug 2026') with the ID secondary. Show the link target as a labelled link ('Wave drop on 6529.io'). Remove the raw RFC8785_JCS code and the 'declaration' ID from visible rows.
findings.acceptance_check: No repository path, WP-/PG- code or bare UUID URL appears as a heading, title or field value on the 15 routes; text group headings name an object.

findings.where: texts and record-work-portrait · default · all viewports · en-US
findings.observation: Near-identical labels are listed without a differentiator. Under 6529NM-PG-2026-001 'Conflict at Its Edges' appears five times (differing only in case), and 'Themes and Variations' and 'Themes and Variations #210' repeat across groups. On the Take the Key! page 'Acquisition or program' reads 'Keys and Gates / Keys and Gates', and the Texts list offers 'All texts for Keys and Gates (Acquisition program)', '(Acquisition program . works)' and '(Acquisition program . artists)'.
findings.consequence: A reader cannot choose between rows or tell whether a duplicate is an error.
findings.change: Show the document kind with each text row (Essay, Catalogue entry, Dossier; the record's kind already gives it) and merge the three 'All texts' links into one 'All texts for Keys and Gates'; list acquisition and program on separate labelled lines only when they differ.
findings.acceptance_check: No two rows in a texts group read identically without a visible kind or date; each 'All texts for' target appears once per object.

findings.where: record-work and record-work-portrait · default · all viewports · en-US
findings.observation: Beneath the image the work page stacks five statements: the credit line ('... Licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0.'), 'Rights: CC BY-NC 4.0, with some uses refused.', 'Approved for contextual display in the Museum.', a restatement of the license terms, and 'Shown only after your browser checks the image's SHA-256 against the file index the registry names on-chain.' (repeated on every image page). 'with some uses refused' does not say which. 'Statement type: Stated by the Museum' appears on every page with no meaning for a visitor.
findings.consequence: The caption is long, repeats the license three times and mixes rights, display authority and verification mechanics, so the credit line is lost.
findings.change: One caption: credit line, then 'License: CC BY-NC 4.0 (noncommercial, attribution required)'. Move the SHA-256 sentence into How this is checked and keep a short 'Checked' badge on the image. Rename 'Statement type' to 'Source of statement' or drop it from the visible list.
findings.acceptance_check: Each image page shows the license once, no per-image verification paragraph, and a caption of three lines or fewer at 390 px.

findings.where: record-work-portrait, record-work-noimage, record-decision, record-object · default · all viewports · en-US
findings.observation: Source prose appears unedited in labelled fields: Medium 'photographic submission; final technical and identity state unverified'; Medium 'On-chain generative software associated with an ERC-721 token on Ethereum; Art Blocks records a token hash. Determinism of live behavior has not yet been independently verified.'; Credit line 'Gift of punk6529; Casey REAS; CENTURY #31; ...' (REAS here, Reas elsewhere); the artist shown as 'GulYildiz' on the work but 'Gül Yıldız (GulYildiz)' in the texts; the accession decision Statement is one run-on sentence listing seven accession numbers.
findings.consequence: Mixed caveats, handles and casing make the record look unfinished and inconsistent across pages.
findings.change: Keep Medium to the medium and show caveats on a separate 'Note' line; use the artist's display name on every page (handle in parentheses once); set the Statement to a short sentence ('7 objects accessioned by donation, accepted 1 Aug 2026') with the numbers as links. If the source record is the cause, fix the record, not the page.
findings.acceptance_check: Medium holds only medium; one name per artist across work, artist and texts pages; the decision statement is two lines or fewer at 1440 px.

findings.observation: The first screen explains the mechanism ('The Museum, read from the chain'; hash and Sepolia) and never says what the Museum holds: nothing gives the number of works, that 13 are in the collection, or what Conflict at Its Edges or Keys and Gates are. The section headed 'Object records' lists condition reports, rights statements, decisions and status observations, which are not objects.
findings.consequence: A visitor who wants to find a work gets a verification explanation first, and the label 'Object records' misdescribes its contents.
findings.change: Lead with a sentence of real counts ('13 works in the collection, 16 selected for Keys and Gates, 186 texts') and put the verification sentence second. Rename 'Object records' to 'Decisions, rights and condition reports'.
findings.acceptance_check: The first paragraph names the collection and its counts; the 'Object records' heading names the record kinds it contains.

Plain verification steps in How this is checked, with the worked subject-ID example
Honest 'no still image of this work' copy for generative works, with a link to the Museum site
Separation of 'Works in the collection' from 'Works selected, not in the collection' and the 'Not in the collection' field
Record-kind labels (Accession decision, Condition report, Rights statement) and relation labels such as Created by and Documented by
Distinct states and copy for mismatch, unavailable and deleted records
